subject: URGENT: Wildfire demo — streaming output freeze and surge in 500 errors
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@wildfire.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, priyam.natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Wildfire demo follow-up — intermittent 500s and stream cutoff

Hi Stephanie / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. We noticed during the 11:00AM demo a hard cutoff of the live response after ~18s and then a flurry of 500 errors when retrying. Our client-facing QA flagged it as a showstopper. I attached a quick screenshot and a short set of logs from our demo harness.

Can you confirm whether this is something on Wildfire's side (we're running client SDK v1.3.2) or if it's related to the Redwood endpoint routing? We have a contract review next week and need a timeline for a fix or mitigation.

Alex
Alex Chen
Senior Product Manager, Wildfire AI
attachments: screenshot-stream-freeze.png; server-logs-20260617.txt
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@wildfire.ai>
Cc: priyam.natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-17T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Wildfire demo follow-up — intermittent 500s and stream cutoff

Alex — thanks for sending these. I've forwarded the logs to infra and put Priya on the thread (she owns the account). 

Quick notes from an initial pass:
- The logs show a sequence of 502/500 responses on the proxy layer followed by the websocket connection being closed from our edge.
- We need the raw server log snippets (full timestamps and request ids) — the attachment is helpful but truncated in the demo harness.

Immediate next steps:
1) Priya will triage and pull the full traces + ingress logs.
2) If we confirm a routing/proxy regression, we will escalate to the runtime on-call.
3) We can provision a temporary dedicated stream route (isolated) to reproduce without shared proxy traffic.

Can you share the exact SDK call pattern (headers, keepalive config) used in the demo? If you can paste sample request IDs we can chase the trace immediately.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: priyam.natarajan@redwood.ai
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, Alex Chen <alex.chen@wildfire.ai>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-17T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Wildfire demo follow-up — intermittent 500s and stream cutoff

Alex / team — I pulled the full ingress traces for the timeframe in question. Highlights:
- 2026-06-17T18:59:12Z request id wf-req-88a3 shows an upstream 502 returned by our proxy after 2 retries.
- The client observed a websocket/tcp FIN shortly after; there is a small cluster of concurrent spikes on shard gsa-17 at the same minute.
- Error rates across the cluster went from baseline 0.3% -> 3.1% for ~7 minutes.

I've opened SRV-1289 for the infra team to correlate kernel drop metrics and proxy thread exhaustion. For reproduction, please try the following SDK tweak: set keepalive_period=15s and disable client-side aggressive retries for that session. That will help us distinguish transient proxy pressure vs. payload handling issues.

I'll keep pulling traces and will arrange a live repro with a dedicated route if we can't isolate quickly.

-Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@wildfire.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, priyam.natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-17T12:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Wildfire demo follow-up — intermittent 500s and stream cutoff

Thanks Priya — attaching two request ids from our client harness: wf-req-88a3 and wf-req-88b7. SDK config:
- Client library v1.3.2, websocket transport
- keepalive: default (30s)
- retry: exponential, 3 attempts

We can switch keepalive to 15s and rerun later today. We'd also appreciate a heads-up if you plan to spin up a dedicated route so we can test under identical conditions. This is high priority — there is a live proposal review on Friday.

—Alex
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, priyam.natarajan@redwood.ai, alex.chen@wildfire.ai
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-18T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Exec alert — Wildfire demo SLA risk and mitigation plan

Team / Alex — looping in for visibility. Given the error rate spike and demo-impacting stream freeze, this needs executive attention. Summary of current findings:
- Incident window: 2026-06-17T18:59:12Z–2026-06-17T19:07:00Z — cluster gsa-17 experienced proxy thread exhaustion coincident with a burst of large tokenization requests.
- Customer impact: live demo cutoff and ~3% error rate during incident window.
- Business risk: Wildfire has a contract review Friday; unresolved demo failures risk the deal.

Immediate mitigation we will enact today:
1) Provision isolated dedicated route for Wildfire (temporary, 48h) and share endpoint by EOD.
2) Apply a conservative connection cap and increase proxy worker pool on gsa-17.
3) Run a coordinated repro with Wildfire engineering (we will provide step-by-step harness).

Longer-term asks for infra (assigned):
- Investigate whether kernel-level throttling or file-descriptor exhaustion contributed.
- Add targeted metric alerting for rapid rise in proxy wait-queues.

Alex — we'll send the dedicated endpoint details and a runbook for your team. Priya will coordinate the repro. Jordan, please prepare the customer-facing summary (one-pager) and proposed credit/contingency language we can offer if we don't achieve a clean repro before Friday.

I'll check back in after the dedicated route is live.

Thanks,
David Kim
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
